name: Brunei
why: Small market; Instagram and Google Maps are where Bruneians post and check places.

spots.name: Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque
spots.desc: Open to visitors when it is not being used for prayers (opening times are posted by the gate). The mosque is very welcoming and if your clothes aren't considered appropriate you'll be given a robe upon entry. Remove your shoes before entering and be respectfully quiet inside as there may be some people there meditating and praying. The mosque is visible from around the centre of the city, but the…

spots.name: Istana Nurul Iman
spots.desc: The residential palace of the Sultan. It is usually not possible to enter, yet the huge size of the palace attracts tourists to snap picture in front of the gate. The palace is however, hidden behind the landscapes, so a better picture can be seen in flyers or souvenirs that feature it. The palace opens to the public once a year on Hari Raya Aidilfitri (Eid al-Fitr), when male members of the…

spots.name: Kampong Ayer
spots.desc: The water village is a beautiful sight to see hundreds of houses seemingly floating on water. The village, which is the world's biggest settlement on stilts, has been on the river for over one thousand years and was the capital of the Bruneian Empire. The water village people are very friendly and many open up their homes to visitors year-round. For a tour by boat, water taxis can be found by…

spots.name: Ulu Temburong National Park
spots.desc: The Ulu Temburong National Park is located in the remote part of the Batu Apoi Forest Reserve. The park covers 550 square kilometers of unspoiled rainforest, the vast majority of which is set off for protection, so visitors are allowed to visit only a small piece. Thanks to Brunei's successful forest protection program, the rainforest in the park has never been deforested. There are no roads, so…

spots.name: Jame'Asr Hassanal Bolkiah Mosque
spots.desc: Another mosque, that resembles Omar Ali Saifuddin Mosque. Whereas Omar Ali Saifuddin mosque is built to commemorate Sultan Omar, this mosque is to commemorate the current reigning Sultan. Visitors, including non-Muslims, can go inside after removing shoes and covering up with a black robe.
spots.hours: Mon-Wed Sat 08:00–12:00, 14:00–15:00; Sun 10:30–12:00, 14:00–15:00; Thu Fri closed (for non-Muslim visitors)

spots.name: Royal Regalia Museum
spots.desc: It displays the royal accessories utilised during the coronation, and some reproductions, as well as gifts received by the Sultan from dignitaries and civilians all around the world. Definitely worth checking out. If you don't have time to visit both, and need to choose between this museum or "Brunei Museum" at Kota Batu, choose this one. Photography is strictly disallowed for the royal treasures…
spots.price: Free entrance for local residents, foreigners pay $5 each (cash only).

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: A lively market in an open-air building. Half of it is full of vendors selling fruit (lots of durian), clothes, and miscellaneous goods. The other half has cheap street food, including sweet drinks and a lot of fried stuff, mostly for $1 each.

spots.name: Brunei Museum
spots.desc: Has unfortunately been closed since 2014 undergoing renovations, and as of January 2026 has not reopened.

spots.name: Malay Technology Museum
spots.desc: This place has many exhibits featuring the different style of houses and lifestyle of those who live on the water village.

spots.name: Tasek Lama Recreational Park
spots.desc: Huge park close to the city with lots of walking trails and a waterfall.

spots.name: Kianggeh Canal
spots.desc: A small canal near the Kianggeh Market, there are sometimes monitor lizards inside the canal and monkeys nearby.

spots.name: Proboscis monkeys
spots.desc: Take a boat along the rivers that snake through the swampy jungle near the capital, and scan the trees to try to spot the monkeys (your driver will look too). Keen eyes help, and bring binoculars if you have them. Also keep your eyes out for beautiful white birds and monitor lizards. Leave at around 17:00 for the best chance of seeing proboscis monkeys—head to one of the waterfront jetties (near…
spots.price: Roughly $15-30 or $10 per person; you might have to haggle a bit

spots.name: Jerudong Park
spots.desc: It was one of the best parks back in 2000s, but these days of glory are faded away long time ago. It got some renovation in 2015 but anyway still some parts of it look abandoned. It consists of two parts: playground and water park.

spots.name: Serasa Beach
spots.desc: Beach got a major face lift in 2015 and now features stylish restaurants, showers, walking trails.

spots.name: The Mall
spots.desc: A good place to shop for supplies, or to check out some local department stores. Surprisingly few multi-national brands. Located in Gadong, it is combined with the Rizqun Hotel. It also has a good souvenir shop.

spots.name: Yayasan
spots.desc: Built by the sultan to support the welfare of the people. Located in central Bandar.

spots.name: Kianggeh Market
spots.desc: A covered market in downtown. You can get Nasi Katok, Teh Tarik, or a kilogram of raw vegetables or sapit.

spots.name: Aminah Arif Restaurant
spots.desc: One of a few local restaurants that features the Bruneian delicacy ambuyat and a pretty good range of other food too.

spots.name: Teng Yun Temple
spots.desc: A smallish Chinese temple.
spots.addr: Jalan Sungai Kianggeh and Jalan Elizabeth Dua

spots.name: Muara Beach
spots.desc: Beautiful beach with food stalls, playground and washrooms.

spots.name: Brunei Products & Souvenir Centre
spots.desc: Souvenir shop downtown near the waterfront.

spots.name: Kawan Restaurant
spots.desc: Located within the row shops. Proper style restaurant with a good mix of Chinese and Malay flavors. Specializes in udang galah (river prawns) and steamboat meals.

spots.name: Teapot
spots.desc: A large teapot monument in the middle of the roundabout of Jalan Pandan Lima, Jalan Singa Menteri, Jalan Seri Maharaja and Jalan Setia Diraja.

spots.name: Old Building of Tutong District Office and Court
spots.desc: An old wooden building which used to house the district office and court for Tutong District.

spots.name: Pantai Seri Kenangan
spots.desc: The popular beach and recreational area in Tutong District. It is located on the spit created by the meanders of Tutong River on its way to the South China Sea.

spots.name: Taman Seri Warisan Emas
spots.desc: A monument to commemorate the 60th birthday of His Majesty Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, the 29th Sultan of Brunei, on 15 July 2006.

spots.name: Tatangan Persiaran Sungai Tutong
spots.desc: A small riverfront promenade along the banks of Tutong River.

spots.name: Times Cineplex
spots.desc: Located in Berjaya Complex, the local cineplex chain provides the only cinemas in the district.

spots.name: Kompleks Pasarneka dan Tamu Tutong
spots.desc: The farmers' market of the town, and one of the main markets in the country. It has wide variety of vendors selling local produce, snacks and even traditional handicrafts. Opens every Thursday from early morning to midday but some vendors may have sold out well before the closing hour so it is best to come at the earliest hours.

spots.name: EasyWay Tea Indulgence
spots.desc: The first bubble tea shop in Tutong. It is now expanded into a cafe.

spots.name: Gerai Selera Pekan Tutong
spots.desc: An open-air food court close to, and overlooking, the banks of Tutong River. The stalls are usually open from dusk and some may last until midnight.

spots.name: Ho Yuen Restaurant
spots.desc: Another established Chinese kopitiam next to Mei Fang and the only non-halal restaurant in town. The restaurant serves popular Chinese dishes such as kolo mee and stir-fried noodles.

spots.name: KK Koya Restaurant
spots.desc: A Malay-Indian Muslim restaurant next to Mei Fang Cafe which is known for its take on rojak, the regional version of fruit and vegetable salad, and may also come with chicken, squid or both. The restaurant in the town is a branch of the original restaurant in Telisai, which is a popular stopover along the old road between Tutong and the towns in Belait District.

spots.name: Mei Fang Cafe
spots.desc: A Chinese kopitiam or traditional coffee shop established in the 1950s and known for its pulut panggang, as well as stir-fried noodles and Chinese desserts. It is usually crowded in the morning.

spots.name: Pasar Malam Pekan Tutong
spots.desc: An open-air building which houses a few food stalls selling popular local snacks such as roti john and kebab as well as takeaways. The stalls are usually open from dusk until night.

spots.name: Puteh Restaurant
spots.desc: A Malay restaurant which is also known for its pulut panggang. The pulut panggang from Puteh Restaurant and Mei Fang Cafe are the most sought after in the district, and perhaps also in the country.

spots.name: Soto Haji Tuah
spots.desc: A food stall established in 1964 and known for its soto. In Brunei, soto is known as a type of noodle soup, that is noodle served in soto, which is an Indonesian-style soup. The stall is in Kompleks Pasarneka dan Tamu Tutong (Tutong Market), the farmers' and fish market in the town.

spots.name: WYWY Restaurant
spots.desc: The restaurant is a branch of a popular restaurant chain the country which has a relatively large variety of menu, especially of side dishes that accompany a rice-based meal. The cuisine is mainly Malay, Chinese and a fusion of both.

spots.name: Ideal Cafe and Grill
spots.desc: A local fast food chain which is known for its grilled chicken.

spots.name: SugarBun
spots.desc: A fast food chain from Sarawak, Malaysia, which is known for its roti john-like fish sandwich. It also serves laksa and beef stew.

spots.name: Par.Tea
spots.desc: A drink stall selling flavoured drinks, shakes and milk tea.

spots.name: The Potato Habit
spots.desc: A local stall chain selling fries which come in various flavours.

spots.name: Restoran Hizadayani
spots.desc: Some local food.

spots.name: Kampong Pandan Mosque
spots.desc: A mosque in the town with a notable Islamic architecture.

spots.name: Jalan Pretty
spots.desc: Original area of the town.

spots.name: Mercu Tanda Kenangan
spots.addr: Jalan Pengiran Haji Ahmad, Jalan Penyurat Haji Abu Bakar

spots.name: Jollibee
spots.desc: A popular Filipino fast food chain.

spots.name: Auntie Anne's
spots.desc: An American chain known for its pretzels.

spots.name: Le Doux Patisserie
spots.desc: A branch of a patisserie from the capital.

spots.name: Mum Bakery and Cake House
spots.desc: A popular local bakery and cake house chain.
